title: Technology of the future
subtitle: nanotechnology, doomsday scenario, global village
summary: Talk about what may be coming - smart homes, keyhole surgery and space tourism, gene therapy and cloning, gridlocked mega-cities and a widening gulf between rich and poor.

lesson.heading: Technology we are likely to see more of
rows: computer-controlled buildings where lighting, heating and security are automatic
travel to planets in outer space, for exploration or for tourism
holidays in space - a company might market two-week holidays on the Moon
the science of developing extremely small tools and machines by controlling the arrangement of atoms and molecules
an operation in which a very small hole is made in the body to reach the organ inside
lesson.note: The adjective smart can be used for anything that uses computers or electronically stored information: a smartphone, a smart TV, a smart car.

lesson.heading: Predicting the future: doomsday and destiny
lesson.text: A **doomsday scenario** is the worst possible prediction of what will happen. Your **destiny** is what will happen to you in the future. To **foresee** something is to think it will occur, and to **envisage** something is to see a possible or probable future situation in your mind.

examples.text: A **doomsday scenario** sees our **destiny** as a world choked with pollution, where many plants and animals have become **extinct**.
The **doomsday scenario** is that we will destroy the world with nuclear weapons.
Many people **envisage** a world in which the poor simply get poorer.

lesson.heading: Cities, population and food
lesson.text: Experts **foresee** a situation where traffic in **mega-cities** - cities of more than 10 million people - becomes completely **gridlocked**, unable to move at all. The **population explosion**, a rapid increase in population, may lead to widespread food and water shortages.

examples.text: Many experts **foresee** a situation where traffic in **mega-cities** becomes completely **gridlocked**.
**Gridlocked traffic** can cost the economy millions of pounds.
Asia underwent a dramatic **population explosion** in the latter part of the 20th century.

lesson.heading: Genes
lesson.text: **Genetic modification**, also called **genetic engineering**, is already used to change fruit and vegetables so that they grow better, but many people object to **genetically modified** (**GM**) food. **Gene therapy** - changing genes in order to prevent disease or disability - will be used to eradicate some diseases, thanks to our knowledge of the **human genome**, the map of all the genes in a human being.

examples.text: The crop had been subject to **genetic modification**.
These **genetically modified** tomatoes will stay fresh for several months.
Scientists now understand how the **human genome** is composed.
Thanks to **gene therapy**, doctors may be able to cure some genetic diseases.

lesson.heading: Designer babies and cloning
lesson.text: **Designer babies** are babies whose genetic characteristics are artificially created. **Cloning** is making a genetically identical copy of an animal or even a human being.

examples.text: Some people **envisage** a world in which **designer babies** will be popular.
**Cloning** of animals, and even human beings, may become common.
This sheep is a **clone**: identical in absolutely every respect to the sheep standing next to it.

lesson.heading: Society and people
lesson.text: The **breakdown** of the traditional family structure has already occurred in some countries, and the **nuclear family** - father, mother and one or two children - may no longer be the main family unit. **Globalisation**, the increase of trade and the spread of similar social behaviour around the world, will grow: the world has become a **global village**, a single community covering the whole world. We may even make contact with **extraterrestrial beings**, creatures from other planets.

examples.text: Since the advent of the internet, the world has become a **global village**.
A typical **nuclear family** is often said to consist of a husband, wife and 2.4 children.

lesson.heading: The gulf between rich and poor
lesson.text: The **gulf** - the gap or difference - between rich and poor nations will widen if we do not take **drastic measures** now. Drastic measures are severe actions that have noticeable effects.

examples.text: The **gulf** between rich and poor nations will widen.
Governments need to take **drastic measures** to save the planet.

lesson.text: Foresee is closer to predict; envisage is closer to picture in your mind. Both are followed by a noun or a that-clause.
